title: The overcounting dichotomy: exact below p, unbounded from p on
content: The parent entry shows the ordinary iterated-derivative multiplicity test is reliable up to order p−1 and blind from p on, and asks: for a GENERAL polynomial, how large is the gap between the multiplicity the ordinary derivatives certify and the true (Hasse) multiplicity m := rootMultiplicity a f? The answer is a sharp dichotomy keyed to whether m reaches the characteristic. If m < p the ordinary test is EXACT (gap 0); if m ≥ p it overcounts WITHOUT BOUND (certifies every multiplicity). No intermediate regime exists — the gap is either 0 or ∞, with the switch precisely at m = p.
mathContext: Ordinary-certified multiplicity $= \max\{n : (\mathrm{derivative}^{[j]} f)(a) = 0 \ \forall j < n\}$. Dichotomy on $m := \mathrm{rootMultiplicity}\,a\,f$: $m < p \Rightarrow$ certified $= m$; $m \ge p \Rightarrow$ certified $= \infty$.

title: The evaluation bridge: ordinary value = k! × Hasse value at a
content: iterate_derivative_eval_eq evaluates the parent scaling identity derivative^[k] f = (k! : F) • hasseDeriv k f at a point a, turning the scalar action into multiplication: (derivative^[k] f)(a) = (k! : F)·(hasseDeriv k f)(a). The proof rewrites with smul_eq_C_mul (a • p = C a * p), then eval_mul and eval_C. This is the pointwise bridge — it lets the factorial threshold (k! : F) = 0 ↔ p ≤ k control the VALUES of the ordinary derivatives at a, which is exactly what a multiplicity test reads.
mathContext: $(\mathrm{derivative}^{[k]} f)(a) = (k! : F)\cdot(\mathrm{hasseDeriv}\,k\,f)(a)$ via $a \bullet p = C\,a \cdot p$, $\mathtt{eval\_mul}$, $\mathtt{eval\_C}$.

title: OrdinaryCertifies: what the ordinary test reports
content: OrdinaryCertifies f a n is the predicate ∀ j < n, (derivative^[j] f)(a) = 0 — 'the ordinary derivatives of order below n all vanish at a', which is exactly the ordinary-derivative test's certificate for (X − a)^n ∣ f. The largest n for which this holds is the multiplicity the ordinary test reports, to be compared against the true rootMultiplicity.

title: m ≥ p: every ordinary derivative vanishes — unbounded overcount
content: unbounded_overcount: if (X − a)^p ∣ f (true multiplicity at least p) then (derivative^[j] f)(a) = 0 for EVERY order j. The proof splits on the factorial threshold: for j ≥ p the whole ordinary derivative derivative^[j] f is identically 0 (parent blindness, ordinary_eval_eq_zero_of_char_le); for j < p the Hasse value (hasseDeriv j f)(a) vanishes because (X − a)^p ∣ f (the Hasse multiplicity criterion), and the ordinary value is j! times it. So the ordinary test never sees a nonzero value; ordinary_certifies_all_of_char_pow_dvd packages this as 'certifies multiplicity ≥ n for every n'.
mathContext: $(X-a)^p \mid f \Rightarrow \forall j,\ (\mathrm{derivative}^{[j]} f)(a) = 0$. For $j \ge p$: $\mathrm{derivative}^{[j]} f = 0$. For $j < p$: $(\mathrm{hasseDeriv}\,j\,f)(a) = 0$ so $(\mathrm{derivative}^{[j]} f)(a) = j!\cdot 0 = 0$.

title: m < p: the ordinary test is exact — gap 0
content: ordinary_exact_below_threshold: if the true multiplicity is exactly m < p — encoded as (X − a)^m ∣ f and (X − a)^{m+1} ∤ f — then the ordinary derivatives vanish at a for all j < m, and (derivative^[m] f)(a) ≠ 0. Below m the Hasse values vanish (criterion), so the ordinary values do too. At order m the non-divisibility forces the m-th Hasse value nonzero; since m < p, (m! : F) is a unit (factorial threshold), so the m-th ordinary value m!·(nonzero) is nonzero. The ordinary test therefore first fails at exactly m, matching the true multiplicity: the overcounting gap is 0.

title: The capstone dichotomy: exactly one regime holds
content: overcounting_dichotomy: for any f ≠ 0 over a field of characteristic p, phrased through the true m := rootMultiplicity a f, EXACTLY ONE of the two regimes holds — exact (m < p: vanishing below m, nonzero at m) or unbounded overcount (m ≥ p: every ordinary derivative vanishes at a). The proof splits on lt_or_ge m p and feeds le_rootMultiplicity_iff (which turns k ≤ m into (X − a)^k ∣ f) into ordinary_exact_below_threshold and unbounded_overcount respectively. The transition is sharp at m = p: no intermediate overcounting gap is possible.
mathContext: For $f \ne 0$, with $m = \mathrm{rootMultiplicity}\,a\,f$: $(m < p \wedge \text{exact at } m) \vee (p \le m \wedge \forall j,\ (\mathrm{derivative}^{[j]} f)(a) = 0)$.

title: Both regimes realized: X^p (unbounded) and X − a (exact)
content: overcount_X_pow: over a characteristic-p field every ordinary derivative of X^p vanishes at 0, while its true multiplicity there is p — the unbounded regime (m = p ≥ p). exact_X_sub_C: for a linear factor X − a, (derivative^[0] (X − a))(a) = 0 but (derivative^[1] (X − a))(a) = 1 ≠ 0, so the ordinary test certifies exactly 1 = the true multiplicity — the exact regime (m = 1 < p). Together they show both sides of the dichotomy are attained by concrete polynomials.
mathContext: $X^p$: $\mathrm{rootMultiplicity}\,0 = p$ yet all ordinary derivatives vanish at $0$. $X - a$: certified $= 1 = $ true multiplicity.
